scenarios.title: Case A: $40 headphones, auto-approved
scenarios.summary: Support's agents look up the order, ask Finance over Nexus, and Finance approves on its own.
scenarios.cost_note: scripted model; Bedrock tokens when the model is live

steps.title: Start Case A
steps.talk: A customer wants $40 back for broken headphones.
steps.point: The ticket at the top, and the first rows in Support's lane.

steps.title: Support discovers Finance's Agent Card
steps.talk: First the A2A discovery: get_agent_card over the finance-agent endpoint.
steps.point: The short wire to the seam: get_agent_card, the one thing Finance publishes.

steps.title: Support asks Finance for the refund
steps.done_when: task.state in [submitted, working, input-required, completed, rejected, failed]
steps.talk: send_message crosses into namespace agent-services. Workers never talk to each other.
steps.point: The wire crossing the seam into Finance's lane: one Nexus call between two namespaces.

steps.title: Finance approves on its own
steps.talk: Under $100 at low risk, Finance's policy approves automatically: approved_by auto.
steps.point: Finance's lane: approved_by auto. No human was needed under $100.

steps.title: Support replies with the refund ID
steps.talk: The answer came back over Nexus, and Support quotes the refund ID.
steps.point: The reply quoting the refund ID. Same run ID from start to finish.
steps.point_versioned: The reply quoting the refund ID, and the pinned Build ID in the header.

scenarios.notes: Support can't move money, so it asks Finance: a different team's agent, through a published contract and a named endpoint. It isn't a child workflow, and only the contract is shared.

scenarios.title: Case B: $450 laptop, a human approves
scenarios.summary: Over $100, Finance's agent asks a human. Support can be switched off while it waits.
scenarios.cost_note: scripted model; Bedrock tokens when the model is live

steps.title: Start Case B
steps.talk: A customer asks for $450 back on a laptop with a cracked screen.
steps.point: The ticket at the top, and the first rows in Support's lane.

steps.title: Finance asks a human
steps.talk: Over $100, Finance's agent says 'I need a human'. The task is input-required.
steps.point: The big state, input-required, and the approval card waiting in Finance's lane.

steps.title: Stop the Support worker (optional)
steps.talk: I switch Support off completely. The Nexus call stays open on the server.
steps.point: The compute rail goes dark: no Support worker runs. Finance keeps waiting; nothing is lost.

steps.title: Approve or reject the refund
steps.talk: I approve as dana.finance.
steps.point: The empty Support rail and the glowing held-open line in the seam, side by side. Then the approval card in Finance's lane.

steps.title: Start the Support worker again (if stopped)
steps.talk: A Support worker comes back and picks the conversation up where it was.
steps.point: A new worker identity in Support's lane, on the same run.

steps.title: Support replies
steps.talk: The reply quotes the refund ID, or apologises if Finance rejected it.
steps.point: The reply quoting the refund ID. Same run ID from start to finish.
steps.point_versioned: The reply quoting the refund ID, and the pinned Build ID in the header.

steps.title: Read the approval report
steps.talk: Support's history went quiet while Finance waited: one Workflow Task recorded that the call started, then nothing until the answer.
steps.point: The report: how long the approval took, and seconds from approval to reply. This run is unversioned: plain workers on support-dev-tq.
steps.point_versioned: The report: lifetimes, one Build ID, and seconds from approval to reply.

scenarios.notes: Over $100, Finance's agent says 'I need a human', and the task goes to input-required. I switch Support off completely. Nothing is lost, and when the approver signals, the conversation picks up again.

scenarios.title: Worker crash: kill Support mid-thought
scenarios.summary: SIGKILL the Support worker while a model turn runs; a new worker carries on from history.

preconditions.label: The console runs the Support worker (so it can kill it)

steps.title: Start Case A
steps.talk: Same Case A. Watch the Support lane: each model turn is an Activity.
steps.point: The ticket at the top, and the first rows in Support's lane.

steps.title: Kill the Support worker mid-thought
steps.talk: kill -9 while the Supervisor is thinking. No graceful shutdown.
steps.point: The rail: the lifetime ends abruptly with a red cut.

steps.title: Start a new Support worker
steps.talk: A new process with a new pid. It replays the history and carries on.
steps.point: A new worker identity in Support's lane, on the same run.

steps.title: The same run finishes
steps.talk: Two workers, one conversation, nothing repeated that had finished.
steps.point: The reply quoting the refund ID. Same run ID from start to finish.

scenarios.notes: Every model call and tool call is an Activity. I kill the process mid-thought, and it carries on from exactly where it stopped.

scenarios.title: Finance outage: Finance disappears mid-call
scenarios.summary: The Finance worker goes away; Support's Nexus call retries until it comes back.
scenarios.cost_note: stops and restarts the console-managed Finance worker

steps.title: Start Case A
steps.talk: Case A again.
steps.point: The ticket at the top, and the first rows in Support's lane.

steps.title: Discovery completes
steps.talk: Discovery is synchronous: Finance must be up for it.
steps.point: The short wire to the seam: get_agent_card, the one thing Finance publishes.

steps.title: Stop Finance
steps.talk: Finance goes away. Nobody polls agent-services-tq.
steps.point: Finance's pip in the stack bar goes down.

steps.title: The Nexus call retries
steps.talk: Attempt 2, 3... with the last failure. Nothing fails on Support's side.
steps.point: The seam: send_message on attempt 2, then 3, with the last failure. Support's code has no retry loop.

steps.title: Start Finance again
steps.talk: Finance is back and the operation completes.
steps.point: The same call completing as soon as Finance is back.

steps.title: Support replies
steps.talk: The customer never knew.
steps.point: The reply quoting the refund ID. Same run ID from start to finish.

scenarios.notes: Finance's team has an outage. Support's call doesn't fail: the server keeps the Nexus operation and retries it. When Finance comes back, the answer arrives.

scenarios.title: AgentCore, you invoke: Case B with a worker built to die
scenarios.sub: Case B; you start each worker lifetime
scenarios.summary: Support's worker is built to die: it starts when invoked and drains when idle. You play the WCI.

steps.title: Start Case B on support-tq
steps.talk: The conversation is pinned to support-supervisor at this Build ID. Nothing polls support-tq yet.
steps.point: The ticket at the top, and the first rows in Support's lane.

steps.title: Invoke the AgentCore app (lifetime 1)
steps.talk: I am the WCI: POST /invocations asks for capacity, not work. Lifetime 1 picks the run up.
steps.point: The compute rail lighting up: lifetime 1. Nothing polled support-tq until the AgentCore app was invoked.

steps.title: Finance asks a human
steps.talk: Over $100, Finance's agent says 'I need a human'.
steps.point: The big state, input-required, and the approval card waiting in Finance's lane.

steps.title: Support's compute drains
steps.talk: Nothing to do, so after the debounce the lifetime drains: /ping is Healthy again.
steps.point: The rail on the left is an empty dashed lane: no Support worker exists. The glowing line in the Nexus seam: the server is holding Support's call to Finance open.

steps.title: Approve the refund
steps.talk: I approve as dana.finance.
steps.point: The empty Support rail and the glowing held-open line in the seam, side by side. Then the approval card in Finance's lane.

steps.title: Invoke again (lifetime 2)
steps.talk: Finance's answer is in Support's history. A new lifetime picks it up.
steps.point: The rail lights up again as lifetime 2 (with the server's WCI, its InvokeWorker row sits on the rail's edge).

steps.title: Support replies with the refund ID
steps.talk: Same build, pinned.
steps.point: The reply quoting the refund ID. Same run ID from start to finish.
steps.point_versioned: The reply quoting the refund ID, and the pinned Build ID in the header.

steps.title: Read the report
steps.talk: Two lifetimes, one Build ID.
steps.point: The report: how long the approval took, and seconds from approval to reply. This run is unversioned: plain workers on support-dev-tq.
steps.point_versioned: The report: lifetimes, one Build ID, and seconds from approval to reply.

scenarios.notes: Support's Worker is now built to die. It starts when invoked, drains when idle, and when Finance answers, a new invocation picks the conversation up, pinned to the exact build.

scenarios.cost_note: scripted model (2 s per turn); Bedrock tokens when the model is live

The console runs the AgentCore app (so it can kill it)
support-supervisor:4ee7f87 is current with local WCI compute

steps.title: Start Case A on support-tq
steps.talk: Case A on the versioned queue. Nothing polls it until the server invokes the app.
steps.point: The ticket at the top, and the first rows in Support's lane.

steps.title: The WCI starts lifetime 1
steps.talk: The server's Worker Controller invoked AgentCore. Watch the model turns in Support's lane.
steps.point: The compute rail lighting up: lifetime 1, started by the server's WCI.

steps.title: Kill the AgentCore app mid-thought
steps.talk: kill -9 while an agent is thinking. On AgentCore this is the microVM going away.
steps.point: The rail: lifetime 1 ends abruptly with a red cut, while a model turn is in flight.

steps.title: Start the app again; the WCI invokes it
steps.talk: The process is back, empty, and I don't invoke it. The unfinished turn times out, the server puts it back on the queue, and its WCI invokes AgentCore.
steps.point: The app is back on :8080 but the rail stays dark: nobody invoked it. About 10 s after the kill (the model turn's heartbeat timeout) the rail lights up as lifetime 2, with its InvokeWorker row on the rail's edge.

steps.title: The same run finishes
steps.talk: Two lifetimes, one conversation. Only the turn that was cut off ran again.
steps.point: The reply quoting the refund ID. Same run ID from start to finish.
steps.point_versioned: The reply quoting the refund ID, and the pinned Build ID in the header.

scenarios.notes: Same crash, serverless shape. I kill the AgentCore app mid-thought and start it again, but I don't invoke it. Temporal sees the turn is unfinished and invokes the app itself, and the run carries on.
